stem: Why are young infants particularly vulnerable to hypothermia compared with older children and adults?

options.A: They have immature thermoregulation and a relatively large body surface area in relation to body size.
options.B: They have fully mature temperature regulation and a smaller surface-area-to-mass ratio.
options.C: They generate unlimited heat through shivering immediately after birth.
options.D: They cannot lose heat through evaporation or convection.

rationale: Young infants have limited thermoregulatory capacity and a relatively large surface-area-to-body-mass relationship, increasing susceptibility to environmental heat loss and hypothermia.
educational_objective: Explain key physiologic reasons infants are vulnerable to hypothermia.
source_locator: Clinical review — infant thermoregulation and high surface-area-to-body-size contribution to heat loss
source_claim_supported: Immature thermoregulation and a large surface-area-to-body-size ratio increase infant hypothermia risk.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13/PDF p.17
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — thermoregulation risk
correction_summary: Narrowed the item to hypothermia vulnerability and removed unsupported claims about infants rapidly gaining heat or adult temperature thresholds.
